samples.summary: Feature ships entirely unreachable: `@yorkie-js/react` is pinned to `0.7.22` while `MinClientKeyVersion` is `0.7.23`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false, both opt-in entry points are hidden and `useDurableDocument` refuses every document. None of the design's Goals ("edits made while disconnected survive a reload") are observable on this branch. The design doc's Rollout section acknowledges this ("PR 4 lands inert... the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), but nothing in the diff bumps the pin, so the entire diff is wiring with no behavior. Worth confirming this is the intended landing state rather than a forgotten bump.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/package.json:66 `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` vs packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`, gating `supportsClientKey()` which gates Settings, the chip offer and `useDurableDocument`.

samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime` is mounted unconditionally by `PrivateRoute` and gated on neither `supportsClientKey()` nor the offline preference. Every signed-in session therefore opens an IndexedDB database, runs the thirty-day sweep, issues an extra `GET /documents` for the revocation reconcile, and lists archives — for 100% of users, including the ones who never opted in and on a build where nothing can ever be stored. That contradicts the design doc's own property: "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing." The cost is an extra request and a DB open per session for everybody.
samples.evidence: src/PrivateRoute.tsx renders `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` unconditionally; offline-runtime.tsx's effect constructs `WafflebaseDocStore`, awaits `retryPendingOfflineErase`, `store.collectStale()`, `fetchDocuments()` and `listRecoverableWork` with no preference/capability check. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Turning it on: "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing."

samples.summary: The design doc (and the new README.md index entry) state that the offline-copy recovery reuses the existing copy engine — "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`" and See Also's "document-copy.md — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". The implementation reuses neither: `recoverOfflineCopy` calls `createDocument` + `applyImportedContent` (the *import* path) and, for notes, a bespoke live-Yorkie-client write. The copy endpoint copies from a server-side source document and cannot take local archive bytes, so the implementation is right and the doc is wrong — but three places now assert a reuse relationship that does not exist, which is exactly the kind of claim a future reader will act on.
samples.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Losing work anyway: "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`"; See Also: "document-copy.md — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses"; docs/design/README.md new row: "over the existing copy engine". packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts imports `createDocument` and `applyImportedContent`, never `copyDocument`.

samples.summary: The design doc states two consequences follow from `durable`: the `beforeunload` guard is suppressed, *and* "the offline-transition toast changes from 'keep this tab open' to 'saved to this device'". Only the first is implemented. The warning toast is gated on `stranded` (`state === 'not-saved'`), so on a durable document no transition toast fires at all — the user is never told their offline edits are safe on disk, they only see a muted chip. Either the doc or the implementation should move; as it stands the documented reassurance does not exist.
samples.evidence: sync-status-chip.tsx:156 `if (stranded) { ... toast.warning('Not saved', ...) }` and `const stranded = state === 'not-saved'`; the durable test asserts `expect(warning).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § What the user sees: "the offline-transition toast changes from 'keep this tab open' to 'saved to this device'".

samples.summary: The design doc promises the recovery notice is phrased "in the vocabulary of the three reasons" (`epoch-reanchor`, `document-purged`, `actor-mismatch`). Nothing stores the `LocalChangesDropped` reason: `expectLoss(docKey)` takes only a key, `ArchiveRecord` has no reason field, and the toast says a single generic sentence ("could not be reconciled with the server") for all three. The user cannot tell a document deleted upstream from a compaction re-anchor, which is the distinction the doc says the message carries.
samples.evidence: offline-runtime.tsx toast description: `Edits to "${title}" could not be reconciled with the server.`; wafflebase-doc-store.ts `expectLoss(docKey: string)` and `interface ArchiveRecord` carry no reason. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Losing work anyway: "The user is then told what happened, in the vocabulary of the three reasons, with a link to the copy."

samples.summary: The doc's "Layout and migration" paragraph specifies an `onupgradeneeded` that relocates existing `toBytes()` envelopes into the snapshot store with an empty change log beside them. The implementation ships `DB_VERSION = 1` with a create-only upgrade arm and an inline comment giving the opposite reasoning ("there is nothing in the wild to migrate... no wafflebase build has ever passed `ClientOptions.store`"). The code's reasoning is sound; the design paragraph describes a migration that does not and need not exist, and a reader planning the next schema bump will be working from it.
samples.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Storage: "An `onupgradeneeded` that relocates each existing value into the snapshot store, with an empty change log beside it, is the whole migration." vs wafflebase-doc-store.ts `const DB_VERSION = 1;` and its `onupgradeneeded` comment "Version 1 creates; there is nothing in the wild to migrate."

samples.summary: A verbatim transcription of the SDK's own test suite (`describe`/`it` imported from vitest) is placed in `packages/frontend/src/lib/` as a plain `.ts` module rather than under a test path or a `*.test.ts`/fixture name. The duplication itself is deliberate and defended in-file (the SDK publishes only `dist`, and it is run against the SDK's `MemoryDocStore` so drift fails in CI), but the layer is wrong: a vitest-importing module sitting in the production source directory is reachable by production imports and by bundling/dead-code tooling.

samples.summary: `api/workspaces.ts` now imports `fetchDocuments` from `api/documents.ts` and performs a client-side listing-plus-filter (`documentIdsIn`) before every workspace delete and every self-removal, to derive local purge targets. This adds an api-to-api dependency and a pre-delete round trip that the design's cleanup table does not describe, and it forced an existing invariant test in `api/url.test.ts` to be weakened from "every request carries the encoded id" to "some request does". An alternative the store already half-supports would be recording `workspaceId` beside each entry so the purge needs no server listing at all.

mergedFrom.summary: The chip's `not-saved` tooltip never names why durability lapsed, which the design makes an explicit requirement

finding.summary: The `Not saved` tooltip never names why durability lapsed, which the design states as a requirement of the new state
finding.evidence: `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` § What the user sees gives a six-row table mapping each cause to a distinct tooltip ('Open in another tab; that one is saving', 'This browser cannot save locally', 'Too large to save on this device', 'Out of local storage space', 'Could not save to this device') and then states: 'Because `Not saved` is now a *designed* state rather than the only state — the second tab, an oversized document, a broken store — ... Its tooltip must name which case applies.' The Risks table repeats it ('Its tooltip names the reason'). `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm implements only a connected/disconnected split plus the opt-in offer; nothing in the chip consumes `persistDisabled`, the store's `onWriteFailure` reason, or the lost-election fact. A user in the second tab of a document with the preference ON — a case this design newly creates — sees the destructive 'Not saved' with 'They exist only in this tab' and no indication that the other tab is saving, and no offer either (`offerOffline` requires `!offlineEnabled`). That defeats the stated purpose of making `durable` a first-class signal rather than a cosmetic one.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing behavior exists. `sync-status-tooltip.ts:29-38` defines `LAPSE_REASONS`, a distinct sentence per cause (`unsupported`, `another-tab`, `dropped`, `too-large`, `out-of-space`, `write-failed`), and `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm appends it at `sync-status-tooltip.ts:109-110` (`const why_not = lapse ? ...` folded into the returned string) — so the arm is not merely a connected/disconnected split plus the offer. The chip does consume the signal: `sync-status-chip.tsx:22,78` imports and calls `useDurabilityLapse()` and passes it to `tooltipFor` at `:266`. The signal is fed by exactly the sources the finding says are unconsumed: `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:199-207` maps `lost -> 'dropped'`, `persistDisabled -> 'too-large'`, `outOfSpace -> 'out-of-space'`, `writesFailing -> 'write-failed'` and publishes it via `DurabilityLapseScope` (`:220`); `collab-document-provider.tsx:257-265,268` supplies the call-site-only causes including the lost election -> `'another-tab'`. The finding's headline scenario (second tab, preference ON, so `offerOffline` is false) resolves to `'another-tab'` and renders "This document is open in another tab, and that tab is the one saving it to this device." independent of `offerOffline`; tests assert this at tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:636-666.

finding.summary: The whole feature is unreachable on the pinned SDK: `@yorkie-js/react` is 0.7.22 while `MinClientKeyVersion` is 0.7.23, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and both opt-in entry points are hidden
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/package.json pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`; yorkie-capabilities.ts sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` and `supportsClientKey()` gates the Settings switch (app/settings/page.tsx), the chip offer, and `useDurableDocument`'s eligibility. As shipped, no user can opt in, so the design's primary Goal — "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload ... on a device where the user has asked for it" — is unreachable on this build. The design anticipates the gate ("Bumping the dependency is the only action needed"), but the Rollout section describes PR 4 as a dark launch "bounded by who turned it on", which presumes somebody can.

verdict.reason: Every factual element of the finding checks out against the tree. packages/frontend/package.json:66 pins "@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22" and pnpm-lock.yaml:728-730 resolves exactly 0.7.22. packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:414-418 injects __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__ verbatim from that pin, and packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,76-82 compares it against MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23" with a strict release-only parser, so supportsClientKey() is false on this build. That false value gates every opt-in surface: app/settings/page.tsx:35, components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.tsx:85, lib/use-durable-document.ts:128, and components/collab-document-provider.tsx:200. No user can opt in, so the design's primary Goal at docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:47-49 is unreachable as shipped. The only plausible refutation would be that the issue sanctioned a dark launch, and while the design doc itself concedes the gate (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:521-531) it also states plainly that "the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped", and the task doc leaves the smoke test unchecked pending the bump (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:220-221, 242-246). That is the design conceding the unmet outcome, not an acceptance criterion permitting it; I cannot establish not-present (code is verbatim as described), already-guarded (the gate is the defect, not a guard against it), or out-of-scope (spec-conformance to the issue outcome is exactly this lens). Uncertainty about the originating issue's acceptance text keeps the finding.
